decks.name: LeetCode #287 - Find the Duplicate Number
decks.description: Find the duplicate number in an array containing n+1 integers where each integer is between 1 and n

cards.question: Find the Duplicate Number: Given an array of integers nums containing n + 1 integers where each integer is in the range [1, n] inclusive. There is only one repeated number in nums, return this repeated number. You must solve the problem without modifying the array nums and uses only constant extra space.

solutions.name: Fast And Slow Pointers (Floyd's Cycle Detection)
solutions.explanation: Treat array as a linked list where each value points to an index. Use Floyd's cycle detection algorithm to find the entrance to the cycle, which is the duplicate number. Most elegant O(n) time and O(1) space solution that doesn't modify the array.

semanticLines: Define function findDuplicate that accepts array nums.
Initialize slow to zero and fast to zero as starting positions.
Start infinite while loop with True to find cycle.
Move slow pointer one step by setting slow to nums at slow.
Move fast pointer two steps by setting fast to nums at nums at fast.
Check if slow equals fast indicating cycle detected.
If equal, break out of loop.
Initialize slow2 to zero as second slow pointer to find cycle entrance.
Start infinite while loop with True to find duplicate.
Move slow pointer one step by setting slow to nums at slow.
Move slow2 pointer one step by setting slow2 to nums at slow2.
Check if slow equals slow2 indicating found cycle entrance.
If equal, return slow as the duplicate number.

solutions.timeDescription: Linear time with two phases: finding cycle and finding entrance, each traverses at most n nodes
solutions.spaceDescription: Constant space using only two pointer variables

solutions.name: Binary Search
solutions.explanation: Binary search on the value range [1, n]. Count how many numbers are less than or equal to mid. If count exceeds mid, duplicate is in lower half, otherwise in upper half. Clever O(n log n) approach using pigeonhole principle.

semanticLines: Define function findDuplicate that accepts array nums.
Store length of nums in n.
Initialize low to one and high to n minus one as value range.
Start while loop that continues while low is less than high.
Calculate mid by adding low to the result of high minus low divided by two using integer division.
Count how many numbers in nums are less than or equal to mid using sum with generator expression, store in lessOrEqual.
Check if lessOrEqual is less than or equal to mid.
If true, duplicate is in upper half, so set low to mid plus one.
Otherwise duplicate is in lower half.
Set high to mid.
Return low as the duplicate number.
codeLines: lessOrEqual = sum(1 for num in nums if num <= mid)

solutions.name: Negative Marking
solutions.explanation: Use array values as indices and mark visited indices by negating values at those positions. When encountering a negative value, that index plus one is the duplicate. Modifies array but uses O(1) space.

Return negative one if no duplicate found.
